A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UDS research and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–F. Retained material can be matched despite additions, relocation, and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B report original fine-tuning accuracy, Pass@1, throughput, component ablations, and parameter-sensitivity results.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds design ablations, alternative training configurations, mathematical-reasoning and distribution-shift evaluations, and an offline-method comparison.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains nuclear-norm scoring, bilinear SRFT projection, FIFO memory, average-distance scoring, and top-K selection. Appendix B.2 evaluates alternative components as ablations without changing the proposed default procedure.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained benchmarks, v2 adds MATH training and evaluation for longer mathematical reasoning, plus evaluations on MATH500 and AMC23 after GSM8K training (Appendices B.4–B.5). These introduce substantial coverage of longer reasoning and explicit distribution-shift scenarios.

E2.justification: Appendix B.7 adds FisherSFT as an evaluated offline comparator across the four original benchmarks, using matched selection fractions. The original Regular, Random, MaxLoss, MaxGrad, RHO-Loss, and GREATS comparisons remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds evaluations with batch size 16, full-parameter fine-tuning, Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, 2048-token MATH sequences, and cross-dataset testing. These supplement the retained main protocols. B.4's blanket statement that previous sequence lengths were 512 conflicts with ScienceQA's retained 256-token setting in Table 18.

E4.justification: v2 substantially extends the original component ablations and parameter sweeps. Tables 7–9 test buffer policies, distance aggregation, and projection constructions; Figures 3 and 9 add norm/rank and Frobenius-norm/utility diagnostics. Further experiments examine robustness across training regimes, longer reasoning, and distribution shifts.

E5.justification: Both versions state four repetitions with different random seeds and report ± values. The additional correlation plots retain the existing Spearman-correlation and p-value reporting approach; no new uncertainty-estimation procedure or increase in repetitions is stated.

E6.justification: Tables 3–4 retain their original values, but Tables 7–15 add substantial results. For example, Table 13 reports MATH accuracy of 46.27% for UDS versus 45.66% for GREATS; Table 14 reports MATH500 accuracy of 42.56% versus 42.27%. Figure 2's correlation trace also changes while retaining its positive trend. Added configurations do not establish same-setting gains over v1.

T1.justification: Lemma 3.1, Theorem 3.2, and the mathematical derivations in Appendix C remain unchanged apart from equivalent notation. The added projection discussion and empirical correlations do not introduce new formal derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about jointly capturing utility and diversity, avoiding external resources, and improving accuracy and training efficiency. The additional evidence does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 adopts correlation wording, and Appendix E newly acknowledges difficulty rigorously proving the nuclear norm's relationship with loss reduction or effective rank. Appendix B.2 adds projection-specific explanations, while B.7 qualifies the offline comparison because throughput is not directly comparable.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 newly specifies default buffer size M=1024 and projection dimensions d1=128, d2=8. Appendix B adds limited implementation and comparison details, including K-means class prototypes and FisherSFT's matched training conditions. The original hyperparameter tables and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion of offline selection methods from Sachdeva et al., Axiotis et al., and Deb et al., plus references supporting the added mathematical benchmarks. The overall online-versus-offline positioning remains stable. FlyLoRA's venue update refers to the same cited work.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section ordering are retained. Changes comprise localized heading and notation edits, brief setup and related-work expansions, and new Appendix B.2–B.7 subsections, without extensive rewriting of the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual evidence with two additional correlation plots and nine new experimental tables. Figure 2 is placed alongside the new Figure 3, and existing tables and figures are redistributed. The original schematic, diversity illustration, selection-budget plot, and sensitivity plots are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses substantial validation gaps in v1 by testing specific design alternatives, full fine-tuning, longer reasoning, distribution shifts, and an offline comparator. These experiments strengthen evidence for UDS's design and applicability; explicit defaults and the added theoretical limitation improve assessability. New experiment settings remain briefly documented and include a sequence-length inconsistency, but the added controlled and robustness evidence provides a substantial net improvement.
